title: Star cluster NGC 6193 and nebula NGC 6188
caption: The star cluster NGC 6193 and the nebula NGC 6188, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The young open cluster NGC 6193 sits at the centre of this view from the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory, with the emission nebula NGC 6188 to its right. Both belong to Ara OB1, a stellar association, and the picture shows one section of it.

An emission nebula is a cloud of gas that glows because it is energised by radiation. Here the ionising radiation comes from the brightest stars nearby, which strip electrons from the gas atoms; when the atoms recapture them, the gas gives off light.

A stellar association is a loose, widely spread group of stars that share a common origin. Young clusters like NGC 6193 and the glowing clouds beside them show star formation in progress, with newborn stars already lighting up the gas around them.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope combines B, g, r and hydrogen-alpha filters. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures and a hydrogen-alpha filter bring out glowing gas far too faint for the eye to see like this.
